title: Sunset v0/completions endpoint and compatibility-layer SDK: PRD, migration plan, and acceptance criteria
creator: Asha Patel
description: Background: The v0/completions REST endpoint and the accompanying compatibility-layer SDK (introduced in 2023 to ease early adopters into our evolving API surface) have accumulated technical debt and block several long‑planned improvements (streamlined parameter validation, structured output enforcement, and unified rate-limiting path). This ticket defines the product requirements, migration expectations, timelines, and acceptance criteria for retiring these interfaces.
scope: In scope: official retirement of the v0/completions REST endpoint and the compatibility-layer SDK packages (python-redwood-compat, node-redwood-compat). Provide migration guidance, SDK redirects, server-side fallbacks for 6 months, deprecation timeline, telemetry to track migration progress, and customer communications. Out of scope: forced client-side package removals, changes to model catalog or pricing, and private on-prem upgrade automation (handled by Private team separately).
goals: Provide a clear, low-friction migration path to the v1/chat and /v1/completions+structured-output endpoints
Reduce runtime maintenance surface by removing compatibility-layer server shim within platform runtime
Ensure >= 80% of active callers migrated or using supported endpoints before hard cutoff
Minimize customer disruption through staged deprecation, SDK helpers, and outgoing support
migration_steps: Phase 0 (Pilot, 4 weeks): Identify top 50 customers using v0 endpoints via telemetry. Offer migration assistance and invite to migration pilot.

Phase 1 (Announcement, week 0): Public deprecation notice (90 days), update docs, create migration guide and quickstart examples for common patterns (simple completion, streaming, stop tokens, logprobs).

Phase 2 (Grace period, 90 days): Serve a deprecation warning header on v0 requests, automatic server-side mapping to v1 where safe (best-effort), and provide SDK patch that emits warnings and surface-breaking-change checks.
Phase 3 (Strict mapping, 180 days): Remove best-effort auto-mapping for ambiguous parameters; v0 returns 400 for deprecated fields. Continue providing migration tooling and targeted outreach.
Phase 4 (Hard cutoff, day 365): Disable v0 endpoint responses. 404 returned. Provide paid migration support for enterprise customers as needed.
timeline: High-level timeline: Announce deprecation 2026-04-01 (90d notice), grace period with soft mapping until 2026-06-30, strict mapping 2026-10-01, hard cutoff 2027-04-01. Dates to be finalized with legal and commercial teams.
acceptance_criteria: Deprecation announcement published on docs.redwood.ai and emailed to org admins and API key owners
Migration guide with code samples (Python/Node/Go) published and linked from deprecation notice
Compatibility-layer SDK packages publish a 1.0.1 shim that shows migration warnings and links to guide
Server telemetry dashboards show per-customer v0 usage and migration status (baseline and weekly delta)
>= 80% reduction in anonymous (non-enterprise) v0 traffic within 180 days of announcement
Engineering sign-off that runtime shim is removable without violating SLOs for remaining traffic
Support playbook and escalation paths published for customers failing migration
rollout_plan: 1) Publish timeline and migration guide; 2) Release compatibility SDK patch that surfaces warnings; 3) Open pilot requests with top customers; 4) Enable server-side warning headers for v0 requests; 5) Transition to strict mapping and generate automated migration tickets for high-value customers; 6) Execute hard cutoff with rollback plan and enterprise migration support on standby.
communication_plan: Multi-channel: (a) docs.redwood.ai deprecation page, (b) email to API key owners and org admins, (c) dashboard banner for accounts with v0 usage, (d) blog post summarizing rationale and timeline, (e) in-console migration CTA linking to migration wizard. Legal/commercial to approve customer outreach scripts for contracts impacted by SLA windows.
metrics: Percentage of API traffic served on v0 vs supported endpoints
Number of migration support tickets opened per week
Number of breaking-parameter errors during strict-mapping phase
risks: Enterprise customers with long upgrade cycles will need bespoke support and may require extended grace-periods
Automatic server-side mapping could mask incompatible behavior leading to silent regressions
Docs/SDKs published late could cause spike in support load at cutoff
Telemetry gaps: if we cannot accurately identify owners of API keys, outreach will be incomplete
mitigations: Reserved enterprise migration windows and dedicated SE time
Conservative mapping: only auto-map parameter combinations with deterministic semantics; otherwise return warnings
Timebox docs and SDK patch delivery; coordinate cross-functional launch checklist
Validate telemetry queries during pilot; enrich telemetry with org metadata from billing
alternatives_considered: Extend support indefinitely: rejected due to maintenance burden and blocking new features
Introduce a formal compatibility SLA and paid extended support: requires legal and ES negotiation; kept as an option for select customers
Deprecate only SDKs but keep HTTP endpoint: inconsistent and confusing for users; rejected
open_questions: What exact billing cutoff terms need to be included for enterprise contracts?
Should streaming semantics from v0 map to v1/chat streaming or be rejected? (runtime/ENG decision)
Can we quantify expected engineering hours for the compatibility shim removal?
Is a migration wizard in-console prioritized for Q2 or Q3?
support_plan: Customer Success: priority triage for orgs flagged as high spend. Offer scheduled migration pairing sessions (2 hours) and dedicated slack channel for pilot customers. Create a paid migration offering for enterprise customers requiring hands-on help.
notes: Avoid using the term 'breaking' in external comms; frame as 'upcoming API consolidation' emphasizing stability and long-term performance improvements. Coordinate with security and compliance on header content to avoid leaking sensitive user info.
post_cutoff_strategy: Maintain readonly access to historical v0 logs for 12 months. Offer a migration audit report for enterprise customers on request. Remove runtime shim entirely after 6 months post-cutoff if no blockers remain.
